title: First Dixieland band to Chicago, recordings, honors and compositions
summary: Brown says he took the first Dixieland band to Chicago, lists the orchestras and Johnny Wiggs records he made, his pet recordings, the Sousa and trophy honors, and tunes he composed.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, Art, they all say that I was the one that took the first Dixieland band to Chicago.

So it must be so. This band was later turned into jazz by Chicago local musicians. Well, we had the finest kind of tempo and rhythm that took the world by surprise and started something really big. That it is all over the world today. I've enjoyed the fruits of jazz since 1950. I made a lot of photograph records which have made hits. I've made some good records with Yerkes. Yerkes, Dance Orchestra. Yerkes, Happy Six. Yerkes, Southern Five. Yerkes, Jazz Marimba Orchestra. Ray Miller's Black and White Melody Boys. The Benson Orchestra. Harvey, Wagonon, Bisonoff, and Johnny Wiggs Orchestra. The best records was with Yerkes Orchestra, some with Ray Miller, one with Brownlee and Chalky, Wofferman Call with Johnny Bisonoff. By the way, folks, I composed this number. I've made over 100 recordings with Johnny Wiggs that I think are very good. I am proud of a lot of these recordings and I am still active in the music world. They won't let me retire, you know. I once played an affair out at the Great Lakes training station alongside of John Philip Sousa for the Navy Boys and received applause from Sousa himself. I was invited to appear on television in acknowledgement of who brought the boys' sticks and land bands to Chicago. We were only allowed 10 minutes and I could not give the complete story to the public in that short time. But my story will always be in print. I received a trophy from the New Orleans Jazz Club and on it was engraved that I was the first to introduce jazz in Chicago. My pet recordings are Tiger Rags, Jazz Band Ball, Fidgety Feet, Clarinet Marmalade, Post-Ms. Lament, Shep Man Tour, all by Johnny Wiggs, Wofferman Call by Johnny Bisonoff, Shake Your Little Shoulder by Harry Yerkes, Rose of Spain by Ray Miller. I composed this one also. And a number of others that are very good and two numbers to mention. I recorded on Janette, Victor, Columbia, Vocalion, OK, Commodore, Tempo, and Southland Long Playing Record. I am still willing to do some more recording. I am proud to see that I compose Moorpomal Blues, which is the foundation of Moaning Blues, Bonyard Blues, Livers Stable Blues. I also compose such numbers as Love Dreams, Rose of Spain, Just Jazz, Baster Street Hop, Tiger Rag, Wolf of Man Call, Wonder Where My Easy Ride Is Riding Now, and others. And I am still composing other numbers.
